item.title: New 6-month programme from WAN-IFRA and OpenAI supports AI-native product development
item.description: Through the AI Futures Lab, newsrooms across Asia-Pacific and Latin America will work on designing and launching news products aligned with their business goals and audience needs.

item.title: Nuevo programa de WAN-IFRA y OpenAI impulsa el desarrollo de productos basados en la IA
item.description: A través del programa AI Futures Lab, redacciones de América Latina y Asia-Pacífico trabajarán durante 6 meses en el diseño y lanzamiento de productos informativos alineados con sus objetivos estratégicos y con las necesidades de sus audiencias.

item.title: AI at work: How newsrooms are redefining production and reach
item.description: AI is moving from experimentation to large-scale deployment as newsrooms shift from testing individual tools to incorporating AI into their editorial and business workflows, says Ezra Eeman, lead of WAN-IFRA’s AI in Media initiative.

item.title: A new cuboid test patch for a fresh approach on print quality
item.description: WAN-IFRA's International Color Quality Club (ICQC) is the worldwide biennial quality competition for newspapers and magazines. Its goal is to improve the quality of reproduction and printing, while also increasing competitiveness as well as training and motivating all personnel.

item.title: Future Newsrooms now: Your input needed to set the standard for transformation
item.description: WAN-IFRA and FT Strategies are embarking on a landmark survey to gauge the strategies, people, processes, tech and focus that will define newsrooms for 2026 and beyond. And we need your input.

item.title: WAN-IFRA announces finalists for the Digital Media Awards 2026
item.description: WAN-IFRA today announced the finalists for the Digital Media Awards 2026 – the news industry's most prestigious global competition celebrating excellence in news publishing.

item.title: ‘Ukraine’s voice in the world’: How the Kyiv Independent keeps ongoing war in the headlines
item.description: Ukraine’s leading English-language newsroom – forged through four years of full-scale war, and now reaching millions of readers worldwide – exists to tell Ukraine’s story and ensure the world does not look away.

item.title: How Sakal is using AI to turn print ads into revenue data
item.description: India’s Sakal Media Group is testing the use of artificial intelligence to turn printed advertisements into structured, searchable data. The company’s director tells us how they use AI-powered OCR to analyse print ads and convert them into data that can be used for sales and revenue decisions.

item.title: The AI content market is taking shape: Four imperatives news publishers must tackle now
item.description: After years of "Wild West" scraping and opaque pricing, a structured and functional marketplace for AI content is beginning to take shape. Insights from a recent WAN-IFRA study tour to San Francisco reveal that by focusing on bot management, data structuring, and collective industry action, publishers can secure their value and influence within the rapidly evolving AI ecosystem.

item.title: When a global story happens in your local community: Steering The Minnesota Star Tribune through unprecedented times
item.description: The new year saw Minneapolis catapulted into international spotlight, with 3000 ICE agents carrying out brutal raids and fatally shooting two people in the street. Steve Grove, CEO and Publisher of The Minnesota Star Tribune, shares how his newsroom navigated the fast-moving, potentially dangerous and often chaotic story of the winter of 2026.

item.title: At The Quint, AI is helping readers navigate long-form journalism
item.description: When readers click into a long investigation, interest doesn’t always translate into attention. For The Quint, analytics showed a familiar pattern: a portion of such readers showed strong traffic to in-depth stories, but weaker engagement post landing.

item.title: AI Integration 101: Lessons in pioneering change management from rural Russmedia
item.description: Lena Leibetseder, Head of Digital Publishing at Austria's Russmedia, provides candid, hard-won and practical insights into what it actually takes to make AI work in a newsroom – and how to bring everyone on board.

item.title: Meeting the audience where they are: How Local News International is rewriting the rules of news delivery
item.description: Dave Jorgenson and Lauren Saks built one of journalism's most successful social media presences at The Washington Post. Now, with Local News International, they're taking that playbook independent – with ‘Zero regrets’.

item.title: WAN-IFRA honours winners of Digital Media Awards Americas
item.description: The 2026 edition of the competition highlighted the most innovative and relevant projects within the digital ecosystem across North America, Central America and South America, once again establishing itself as a benchmark for the industry.

item.title: Martin Schori on hiring for yesterday while bracing for tomorrow
item.description: When did you last hire someone without knowing exactly what they'd do on day one? If the answer is never – or not recently – Martin Schori thinks that's worth sitting with. The future of media may depend less on the roles we define than on the people we keep turning away.
